headline: NAB's cash earnings were broadly stable in FY25, decreasing $11m or 0.2% to $7,091m from $7,102m in FY24 (ev-7, ev-10, ev-37). Net operating income rose 2.9% to $20,813m (ev-40, ev-16); underlying profit (income less operating expenses, before impairment) rose 1.3% to $10,965m from $10,823m (ev-39, ev-36). Statutory net profit attributable to owners fell 2.9% to $6,759m from $6,960m (ev-9, ev-38); statutory net profit from continuing operations fell $275m to $6,788m (ev-8). The cash-to-statutory gap reflects non-cash items: hedging and fair value volatility +$28m after tax, amortisation of acquired intangibles -$36m, and acquisitions/integration/disposals/business closures -$295m after tax (ev-33, ev-34, ev-35). The $11m cash earnings decline is the net of NII +$644m, other operating income -$67m, underlying operating expenses -$305m, notable payroll review/remediation -$130m, credit impairment -$105m, and tax/NCI -$48m.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $644m or 3.8% to $17,398m, including a $74m decrease from economic hedge movements offset in other operating income; underlying increase of $718m or 4.3% from higher AIEA (+$22.5bn or 2.3%) and NIM (+3bps to 1.74%). NIM driven by higher earnings on deposit/capital replicating portfolios (+9bps), lower HQLA mix (+2bps) and M&T (+2bps), offset by higher deposit costs (-7bps), higher wholesale funding (-2bps) and lower lending margin (-1bp).

Other operating income decreased $67m or 1.9% to $3,415m. Net fees and commissions down $132m (incl. $102m customer-related remediation vs $35m FY24 and $66m fee reduction from business disposals); trading income up $33m (incl. $74m economic hedge movements offset in NII); other income up $32m (MLC Life, FirstCape NZ).

Operating expenses increased $435m or 4.6%; excluding $130m payroll review and remediation, up $305m or 3.2%. Personnel +$271m (ex $101m payroll review, +$170m), technology +$71m, general +$81m (ex $29m, +$52m), occupancy +$12m. Driven by salary inflation, technology/financial crime investment and additional bankers, partially offset by productivity benefits and lower EU/AUSTRAC costs.

Credit impairment charge increased $105m or 14.4% to $833m, driven by a higher individually assessed charge (+$328m to $964m) primarily in Corporate and Institutional Banking, partially offset by a lower collective charge (from a $92m charge to a $131m write-back, -$223m).

Income tax expense increased $27m or 0.9% to $3,002m due to higher cash earnings before income tax and a higher effective tax rate. Non-controlling interests increased $21m (from $18m to $39m). Combined negative contribution of $48m.

Payroll review and remediation costs of $130m in FY25 (FY24: $nil) are included within operating expenses and stated separately as a notable item. Excluding these, operating expenses rose $305m or 3.2%.

notable_items: Payroll review and remediation costs of $130m in FY25 (FY24: $nil), included within operating expenses
limitations: The NII volume/margin split is not quantified in dollars by the bank (only NIM in bps and AIEA growth in $bn), so NII is claimed as a single component at +$644m.

The tax_and_other component combines the bank-stated tax movement (+$27m) with a non-controlling-interests delta (-$21m) computed from the two period columns; the NCI delta is my arithmetic, not a bank-stated movement.

The investor presentation's operating-expenses bridge (page 36) and P&L indicators (page 21) describe the half-on-half (2H25 vs 1H25) comparison, not the FY25 vs FY24 task comparison, so they are context only and were not used for contributions.
The $130m payroll review and remediation costs are disclosed as a notable item within operating expenses; the underlying operating-expenses contribution of -$305m excludes them.
Capped at 80: tax_and_other -48 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
